summary: Both supplied occurrences were examined. The existing 70/56 example already gives reciprocal human destruction. mt- is part of the inherited active base mtawlafle/mtawləf here; neither its shape nor ḥḏoḏe licenses Detransitive classification.

The book-destruction context in Talay 2/7 supports the existing broad destruction meaning. It does not independently establish a technical book-burning sense, and the text distinguishes burning from later gunfire destruction.

The new surface form mtawlfənne has a reduced stem and suffix sequence not transparently equivalent to inherited Preterit mtawlaffe. Narrative German tense alone is insufficient to choose a Turoyo box; it is withheld as an example pending segmentation.

Allowed form lookup identified both tlf and twlf as consonantal candidates. The tlf entry has distinct inherited forms taləf/toləf, mtalafle/mtaləf and matlafle/matləf. Overlapping destruction semantics do not justify merging the roots or changing the current stem I label.
No new base forms, sense numbers or idioms are inferred from the two records.
How is mtawlfənne at Talay 2/7 segmented, and is it Preterit or Infectum in the surrounding procedure? Confirm agent and patient marking before adding it to a form box.
What is the historical and synchronic relation of twlf mtawlafle/mtawləf to tlf II/III? The unknown etymology in the current entry is retained.
Does the text’s unprefixed coordinated form reflect a locally regular narrative pattern? Its German tense alone does not settle the morphology.

Talay 2/7 describes destruction of books, an inanimate patient extension of vernichten rather than a separate sense. The finite box of mtawlfənne remains unresolved, so the passage is retained as evidence here without a box example.
